title: Credits and Refunds Set Against the Cost of Coming Home
content:
A credit or a refund the carrier granted is not money out of the traveller's own pocket, so what the
traveller paid to come home on an interruption claim under the Travel Protection Plans is reduced by it. Both
lines are read from the carrier's ledger of the traveller's air bookings held under the Air Ticket Fare Brands.

## The three readings

1. Where a travel credit stands redeemed on the traveller's bookings and something was charged for the return
   home, what the traveller paid to come home is reduced by the credit redeemed, because a credit the carrier
   granted is not money out of the traveller's own pocket.
2. Where no travel credit stands redeemed and the carrier has refunded part of the fare on an airline
   cancellation, what the traveller paid to come home is reduced by that refund.
3. In every other case what the traveller paid to come home stands at what the carrier charged for it.

Under either of the first two readings the result is never less than nothing: where the credit redeemed or the
refund comes to more than what was charged for the return home, what the traveller paid to come home is nothing
rather than a negative figure.

## Worked through on hypothetical figures

Charges of 817.10 for the return home against a travel credit of 300.00 redeemed on the traveller's bookings
leave 517.10 under the first reading. The same charges with no credit redeemed but 250.00 refunded by the
carrier on an airline cancellation leave 567.10 under the second. The same charges with neither a credit
redeemed nor such a refund stand at 817.10 under the third. A credit of 900.00 redeemed against charges of
817.10 leaves nothing.
